It's more Spider-man...but also isn't.

The second installment just doesn't have the same heart that the first game had.
-Things that were added either shouldn't have been, or they had minimal impact.
-And a lot of things were removed that shouldn't have been.

-The story pacing is rough in some parts. It feels like about ~5 hours were missing/cut. It probably wasn't critical, but it would've helped tremendously in the middle to back half of the game.

-NPC and world interactions are also reduced, leaving a feeling of emptiness. Yeah things like seamless loading from fast travel is a neat feature, but honestly, I really liked seeing Spider-man have to take the subway. (It was a small thing, but it was so humanizing. It really gave the feeling of a "friendly neighborhood Spider-man." And the implied stories the loading screens gave as the people of New York interacted with him were always enjoyable.)

It's little changes here and there that make the game feel less like a passion project, and more like an obligation.

It's not a fantastic game, but it's not bad either. It's...underwhelming.

It's unquestionably more of a sequel and standalone game than Miles Morales. But if they went 0-100 miles in the first game, they only went about another 35 here.

Here's to hoping that they bring back the magic in the next game.

I played it on PlayStation 5 and I thought it was alright i played it like 2 years ago but this PC version is a terrible port. Do not buy this for Steam Deck very misleading by Valve, Insomniac and Nixxes marking this as "Verified." It is completely unplayable on Steam Deck. The frame rate constantly dips into the low teens. The audio crackles and cuts out during cutscenes. Turning the graphics down to the absolute lowest settings makes the game look like a blurry PlayStation 2 mess and it still stutters. Swinging through the city causes massive freezes every couple of seconds. I put around a hour and a half into this trying to tweak the settings to make it look fine but nothing works. It's crazy how this passed verification. Avoid it until it gets a massive performance patch But since Sony doesn't want to put their PlayStation exclusive single player titles on PC anymore, I doubt this will get fixed lmao.

Story fell apart for me in the last act. Writing has taken a nose dive since SM1, and a lot of the Miles content suffers--which is a shame, because he's a great addition to the game overall. Last act was so bad I can't recommend it.

By the way, if you own a DualSense Edge, please know that Sony fumbled the PC implementation and none of the DualSense's advanced features will work (not just here, but anywhere on PC). The paddle buttons integrate nicely with Steam and can be directly programmed via Steam input. Haptic feedback and responsive triggers work on the base model Dualsense (complete with all of that controller's durability issues), but not on the Edge. This is more of an issue with that specific controller, but it's worth mentioning here since I believe the game does greatly benefit from haptic feedback and responsive triggers. Selling the Edge as PC compatible and marketing those features, then not actually implementing those features on any of your flagship PC ports, is insane.

If you do decide to play this game, simply use a regular Dualsense if you have it and do not install Sony's software. The game will natively detect your Dualsense, but Sony's software will add another layer of emulation which breaks it.

35 hours for:
- Main Story
- Side Missions
- Collectibles
- Photos
- Challenges

Basically everything. Except a couple of hidden achievements which I missed, hence the extra 2hours added. 

One MAJOR flaw for me is, you need to play NewGame+ to get 100% achievement. 
Which REALLY SUCKS. Because there's a few cutscenes that you CANNOT skip. 
And for those that you CAN skip, you need to Press ESC > Skip Cinematic each and every time. Annoying.

Stick to the 1st game. Because this one, what it offers is a stark decline in plot, characters, gameplay and player experience through and through.
From top to bottom the worst aspects of this game:
1. Ultra-level moral preaching in almost all aspects of the story, main missions, side-quests, in the manner of "we are going to shove it down your throats and you will say thank you".
2. undeniable proof that Miles Morale's spider-man is purposefully placed in the story to usurp everything about the real, true and only spider-man, Peter Parker. And let's give him a crazy amount of ridiculous super-powers BECAUSE...
3. making Harry the Venom is so childish. It destroys the real Spider-man/ Venom canon. This game manages to make Sam Raimi's Spider-man 3 look like a masterpiece.
3. All side-quests are stupid and boring.
4. web swinging feels so arcade-y compared to the first game.
5. combat is very bland

Final thoughts: hopefully the developers will never be able to make another spider-man.

tldr.text: Very Positive (83%): players love the story and characters, the thing they praise most.
The main complaint is bugs and crashes, the most common gripe in the reviews.

details.text: Bugs and crashes come up less in recent reviews, with 13% of them raising it against 23% over all time.
Players who reviewed after very little playtime are far less positive than those who logged very long sessions.
